subject: D1CA07BA971AE54EB4BCE0ABB94841E7
introduction: “True reliance,” Bahá’u’lláh writes, “is for the servant to pursue his profession and calling in this world, to hold fast unto the Lord.” The guide begins there, and with ‘Alí on the rooftop refusing to prove his trust by jumping: trust in God gets to work and uses the means. From that beginning the readings go on to trustworthiness; to courage that stays careful; to grief; to contentment and the heart’s one lasting attachment; and to a long series of short letters and prayers, written to people in exile, illness, debt and danger, that say again and again, “Grieve not. Put thy trust in God.” The Psalms carry most of the outside quotations, as they have carried this trust for three thousand years, with Proverbs, Job, Isaiah, the Sermon on the Mount, Paul’s shipwreck and the Qur’án’s “whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.” Some texts speak against the readings or test them. Emerson and Henley trust themselves; Voltaire and Marx object to resignation; the psalmist asks why; Ecclesiastes sees time and chance; and the three at the furnace add “but if not.”
questions: “True reliance is for the servant to pursue his profession and calling.” Why do the readings begin a guide on trust with work? What idea of trust are they heading off?
‘Alí would not jump, Jesus would not cast himself down, and Paul said the sailors must stay with the ship. State the rule these three stories share.
“Our God is able to deliver us … but if not.” Is trust in God a belief about what will happen? If not, what is it?
“Grieve not,” say dozens of these letters, and Jesus wept. How do you read the command so that it comforts and does not silence?

Marx says resignation keeps the oppressed quiet; Voltaire refuses to call a disaster good. How do the readings’ own demands for effort, justice and care answer them, and what do the critics still have a right to ask?
“None is aware of that which can harm or profit him.” Recall something you wanted and are now glad you did not get. What does that memory do for trust?

outside.why: “True reliance is for the servant to pursue his profession and calling.” Proverbs holds effort and trust in one line: the horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.
The Bhagavad Gita: let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.

‘Alí on the rooftop is dared to throw himself down if he trusts God’s protection. Jesus on the pinnacle of the temple met the same dare, with a psalm quoted in its support, and answered: thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
Paul had been promised that no life would be lost in the wreck. When the sailors tried to slip away he said: except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved. The promise did not excuse the means.
“Striving and endeavor … are necessary and obligatory.” Nehemiah: we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night.
“One must hold fast to the means while placing one’s trust in God.” Jacob in the Qur’án gives his sons a prudent plan and adds: I can naught avail you as against Allah. In Him do I put my trust.
Means and trust together. Poor Richard keeps the first half: God helps them that help themselves. What does the proverb leave out that the readings insist on?
“Put thy trust in the Lord of all causes.” A psalm: it is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in princes.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án. The verse: whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.
“What conforms with divine decree will be realized.” Proverbs: a man’s heart deviseth his way: but the Lord directeth his steps.
James to people with confident business plans: ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

“None is aware of that which can harm or profit him.” The Qur’án: it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not.

“Renounce the promptings of your own will.” Emerson built his best-known essay on the opposite counsel: trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string. Which of the self’s promptings does each have in view?
The exiles lived so that “all the inhabitants began to trust them in all their business.” Jesus: he that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
Conduct such that “all people of the world, from kings to subjects, will trust.” Jesus: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
“You proved trustworthy.” The master in the parable: well done, thou good and faithful servant.

God offered his Trust to all, and “none bore it.” Bahá’u’lláh alludes to this verse: We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it. And man assumed it.
“Unto Him do all matters return.” A psalm: I trusted in thee, O Lord: my times are in thy hand.
“He is with thee and will aid thee and protect thee.” Isaiah: fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God.
Our “recognition of our powerlessness” is the means of approach. Paul: my strength is made perfect in weakness.

Powerlessness confessed. W. E. Henley, from a hospital bed, said the opposite and meant it: I am the master of my fate, I am the captain of my soul. What does each stance make possible, and what does each risk?
“He is with thee and knoweth what thou art upon.” A psalm that admits the fear first: what time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
“Fear thou no one.” A psalm: the Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
“Exercise the utmost care and wisdom in all affairs.” Jesus: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
“These days more bitter than poison shall pass.” A psalm: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.

Under investigation, “we trust in divine protection and the justice of His Imperial Majesty.” Paul, a prisoner on a sinking ship: be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

Trust in protection. The three before the furnace added two words that change the meaning of trust: our God is able to deliver us; but if not, we will not serve thy gods. Is the trust in these readings a confidence that harm will not come, or something that holds if it does?
A prayer on leaving the city. The traveller’s psalm: the Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in.
“Unto God do I commit My affairs and your affairs.” A psalm: cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.
“He is nearer to thee than thyself.” The Qur’án: We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
“It is not for me … to say, whence is this to me or wherefore hath it happened.” Job on the day he lost everything: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.
The handmaid does not ask why. The psalmist does, and the Bible kept his question: my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Is asking “why” a failure of trust, or one of its forms?
“He will … protect thee.” Moses’ last blessing: the eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms.
“I have committed my affairs unto Thee.” A psalm: commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
“Grieve thou not over anything.” Jesus on his last evening: let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
Grieve not. The same Gospel records that Jesus wept at a friend’s grave. How do the readings in this part make room for sorrow while counselling against grief?
“The heart must have some attachment,” and all else is destined to perish. Jesus: where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
“While a man is happy he may forget his God; but when grief comes … then will he remember his Father.” The prodigal among the swine: I will arise and go to my father.
“He is more kind than a father.” Jesus: if ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven?
Turning toward God “is the healing of the body, the mind and the soul.” Isaiah: in returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength.
“Whatever comes to pass should be considered the essence of wisdom.” Paul: all things work together for good to them that love God.
Joseph to the brothers who sold him: ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.

Whatever happens is wisdom. Voltaire wrote against exactly that after an earthquake killed tens of thousands in Lisbon: yet in this direful chaos you’d compose a general bliss from individuals’ woes? What may a person say of his own trials that he should hesitate to say of another’s?

Joy in all conditions is “impossible unless thou holdest fast unto absolute reliance upon God.” Paul: be careful for nothing; and the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds.
“Resignation to the Will of God is the soul of happiness.” Paul: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

Outward conditions will not disturb a resigned soul’s peace. Marx saw in that peace the reason bad conditions last: religion is the sigh of the oppressed creature; it is the opium of the people. The first readings of this guide command work and striving. Is that answer enough?
“He doeth as He doeth, and what recourse have we?” Job: though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
He “turneth trouble into ease.” The Qur’án: lo! with hardship goeth ease.
“He aids whomsoever He wishes to serve His … Cause.” Paul, after being pressed beyond his strength: that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead.
“Thou seest me clinging unto Thee.” A psalm: he shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust.
“Hold fast to the Sure Handle.” The Qur’án: whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold.
“He will help thee as He helped thee before.” Samuel set up a stone and named it for past help: hitherto hath the Lord helped us.
All will be “questioned concerning what your hands have wrought.” Jesus’ story of a man who trusted his barns: thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee.
Jeremiah draws the two kinds of trust as two plants: the heath in the desert, and a tree planted by the waters, that shall not be careful in the year of drought.
“Whether traveling or at home, and in my occupation or in my work, I place my whole trust in Thee.” Proverbs: in all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
A prayer to have ordained what is best. Jesus: not as I will, but as thou wilt.
“Aid me, at all times, to put my trust in Thee.” A psalm: wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart.
“My gaze hath, at all times, been fixed on the horizon of Thy gracious providence.” King Jehoshaphat before an invasion: neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.
Confidence in his bounty “emboldeneth me … to ask.” The Letter to the Hebrews: let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace.
“Say: God sufficeth unto me.” The Qur’án’s form of the same words: Allah is sufficient for us! Most Excellent is He in Whom we trust!
Face turned, hands clinging. A psalm: I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother.
A prayer for the living waters. A psalm: as the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee.
“None hath any refuge save Thee, nor any path except unto Thee.” Peter, when others were leaving: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.
“Thou art My sole Companion in My loneliness.” The shepherd psalm: though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me.
On meeting opponents: “Sufficient is God unto me.” God to Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh: fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, hearing and seeing.
“Detach thyself from all else but Him” in days of the world’s intoxication. The First Letter of John: love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
“Not an atom’s weight escapeth His knowledge.” Jesus: one sparrow shall not fall on the ground without your Father. The very hairs of your head are all numbered.
“Be content with whatsoever God hath been pleased with.” The Letter to the Hebrews: be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án here. Pickthall’s rendering: if Allah is your helper none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you?
Events in the prison are “from the hidden ordinances.” The Qur’án: say: naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us. He is our Protecting Friend.
“Fear no one … He will protect thee from the hosts of Satan.” King Hezekiah under siege: with him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the Lord our God to help us.
Whoever trusts completely “shall fear no one.” A psalm: he shall not be afraid of evil tidings: his heart is fixed, trusting in the Lord.

In tribulations “there shall be revealed that which lies hidden therein” of wisdom. Julian of Norwich, in a century of plague: all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well.

Hidden wisdom in every trial. The Preacher looked at how things fall out and saw no pattern: the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; but time and chance happeneth to them all. How does a person trust a wisdom he cannot see without pretending to see it?
“The test and trial is severe.” Jesus to Peter: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
“Patience is called for, and long-suffering, and trust in God.” Lamentations: his compassions fail not. They are new every morning. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait.
Occupy thyself with remembrance; “He will protect thee.” A psalm: he that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
“Fear no one.” A psalm written in flight: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord sustained me. I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people.
“He knoweth you better than your own selves.” Jesus: your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
“Be steadfast in thy Lord’s Cause.” Paul: be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.

“I have remained alone, and I have taken for Myself no helper save God.” Paul from his last prison: at my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me. Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me.
“Commit thy affairs unto Him.” The First Letter of Peter: casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
“Let nothing grieve thee.” Jesus: peace I leave with you; let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
“Trust in Him - He sufficeth thee.” Jesus: take therefore no thought for the morrow. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
“Remember Him at eventide and at dawn.” A psalm: at midnight I will rise to give thanks unto thee.
“Be of good cheer,” sent from the Most Great Prison. Jesus, hours before his arrest: be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
“Every desire will be fulfilled.” Jesus: ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find.
Every desire fulfilled. James is cooler about what desire asks for: ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss. Which desires does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s sentence have in view?
“He is the Hearer, the Answerer.” A psalm: call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee.
“Grieve not over anything in this world.” Habakkuk, with the fields empty: yet I will rejoice in the Lord.
“In every matter seek assistance … through the unseen aid.” A psalm: he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
“God thy Lord loveth those who put their trust in Him.” Proverbs: whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy is he.
“He shall manifest unto thee that which He hath willed.” Isaiah: they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.
“Be not grieved by the disorder of outward affairs.” The disciples in the boat: he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still.
“He bestoweth that which is befitting.” Proverbs: trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
“Be patient within thyself.” James: ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
Commit all to Him, who executes what wisdom requires. Hamlet, near the end: there’s a special providence in the fall of a sparrow. The readiness is all.

Commit every matter to God. Helena in All’s Well: our remedies oft in ourselves do lie, which we ascribe to heaven. The guide’s first reading would agree that the remedy must be used. Where does committing a matter to God end and neglecting it begin?
“Say always in the name of God - and rely upon Him.” Proverbs: commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.
What makes the love of God grow is “to turn one’s self toward God.” James: draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.

psalm-cast-thy-burden-upon-the-lord.text: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved

exodus-stand-still-and-go-forward.text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. And the Lord said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward

psalm-what-time-i-am-afraid.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee. In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me

psalm-better-to-trust-in-the-lord.text: It is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in man. It is better to trust in the Lord than to put confidence in princes

proverbs-horse-is-prepared.text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord

jeremiah-blessed-is-the-man-that-trustet.text: Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord. For he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited. Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit

lamentations-his-compassions-fail-not.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord

john-let-not-your-heart-be-troubled.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me

corinthians-not-trust-in-ourselves.text: For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us

chronicles-our-eyes-are-upon-thee.text: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee

chronicles-an-arm-of-flesh.text: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him: With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles

genesis-god-meant-it-unto-good.text: And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive

psalm-my-times-are-in-thy-hand.text: But I trusted in thee, O Lord: I said, Thou art my God. My times are in thy hand

psalm-i-laid-me-down-and-slept.text: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord sustained me. I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about

quran-whosoever-putteth-his-trust-he-wil.text: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things.

quran-if-allah-helpeth-you-none-can-over.text: If Allah is your helper none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you after Him? In Allah let believers put their trust.

quran-naught-befalleth-us-save.text: Say: Naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us. He is our Protecting Friend. In Allah let believers put their trust!

quran-no-beast-but-its-sustenance.text: And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah. He knoweth its habitation and its repository. All is in a clear Record.

acts-except-these-abide-in-the-ship.text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship, Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved

acts-i-believe-god-that-it-shall-be.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship. For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee. Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me

samuel-ebenezer.text: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us

proverbs-commit-thy-works.text: Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established
